metadata.description: Source positions: reserved span annotations on parsed terms, resolution of a SubtermPath to a span, and conversion of codepoint offsets to (line, column) positions.

literal.string: Annotate an application term with the span running from the start of its function to the end of its argument, when both have spans; otherwise leave it unannotated
Wrap a term in a layer whose only annotation is the reserved span key. This is surface trivia, like comments: it is exempt from the round-trip contract and is removed by stripSpans.
Reserved annotation key for source spans recorded by the textual parser

Convert a codepoint offset within a text into a zero-based line and a zero-based column counted in UTF-16 code units (the Language Server Protocol's convention). Lines end at LF, CR, or CR LF; an offset beyond the end of the text is clamped to the end.
Remove span-only annotation layers from the top of a term, leaving the term itself

Resolve a subterm path (as carried by type-checking errors, computed on the span-free term) against a span-annotated term, returning the span of the node it reaches. If the node itself has no span, the span of its nearest enclosing node that has one is returned; if the path cannot be followed, the span of the last node reached.
Resolve a list of subterm steps against a span-annotated term; see spanAtPath
Decode a span from its annotation value, a pair of int32 literals (start, end)
If a term is a span-only annotation layer (see annotateSpan), return its span and the term it wraps
Encode a span as an annotation value: a pair of int32 literals (start, end)

Remove every span-only annotation layer from a term, including those inside user annotation payloads. Applied to a freshly parsed term, this yields exactly the term that parsing without spans produces.
Follow a single subterm step from a (span-free) term to the immediate subterm it names, if the term has that shape. Map-entry and set-element steps depend on a term ordering and are not resolved.
The source span recorded on a term by the parser, if the term's outermost layer is a span annotation
